newsitem.title: USA: U.S. swap spreads widen in two-year area.
newsitem.headline: U.S. swap spreads widen in two-year area.

text.p: The two-year area in U.S. interest rate swap spreads stayed well bid on Friday after gradual gains in the past few days, traders said.
The two-year was bid at 31-1/2 basis points and offered at 32-1/2, compared with 29 bid/30 offered on Wednesday.
Several million dollars in notional value was said to have traded at 32 bps today, perhaps the widest level in years, traders said.
A U.S. bank trader on the West Coast said the widening was part of a long-term change in the supply/demand across the curve due to reductions in the U.S. Treasury's note offerings.
"The primary motivation is belief that short-dated Treasuries will appreciate because of the scarcity value, because the Treasury is going to curtail certain issues," he said.

"It probably will also influence five- and 10-year spreads," he added. "A lot depends on what the Treasury eventually do with their five-year financing. If we go to quarterly (from monthly auctions), I think you'd see five-year spreads move out five, six or seven ticks easily."

On the other hand, a swaps broker in New York said the widening in the two-years might be a more temporary movement linked to the settlement of August Treasury bond futures options on the Chicago Board of Trade today.
Traders said some consolidation in the swaps curve was likely next week, perhaps taking cue from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.
Still, the longer end of the curve was mostly steady throughout the past week.
The 10-year spread was quoted at 38-1/4 bps bid versus 39 offered, roughly unchanged on the week.
In swaptions, a big at-the-money straddle was said to have traded in 10-year maturities on 10-year spreads.
"Other than that, vols (implied volatilities) look slightly bid out there, but it's been pretty quiet overall," a Japanese bank trader in New York said.
